findings.reason: The authentic original screenshot has no illustration. A sideways parabola with two marked preimages materially explains why projection to the natural parameter is not locally injective across the fold, beyond the algebraic verification.
findings.action: Appended a final Remarks section with an independently justified TikZ sketch of the solution curve, its fold, and projection of two distinct points to the same positive parameter.

correction: Added the warranted fold/projection illustration only. Original title, complete Example, Facts, Verification, frontmatter, sources, dependencies and publication status are byte-identical.

diagram_math_checks.objects: C={(lambda,x) in R^2:lambda=x^2}; horizontal coordinate lambda, vertical coordinate x.
diagram_math_checks.check: The parametric plot (t^2,t) satisfies lambda=x^2 at every displayed point; it has both positive and negative x branches and only the origin on lambda=0.
diagram_math_checks.local_justification: Example equation and Verification step 1.1 give exactly lambda=x^2.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Projection pi:C -> R, pi(lambda,x)=lambda; drawn on the horizontal lambda-axis.
diagram_math_checks.check: For every sufficiently small a>0, (a,sqrt(a)) and (a,-sqrt(a)) are distinct points of C and both map to a. Dashed arrows point from the two curve points toward (a,0); the latter depicts the axis representative of the scalar a and is not a third solution point. Unnumbered schematic axes permit scaling lambda by a and x by sqrt(a); plotted normalized marker positions (1,+/-1) give the stated pair.
diagram_math_checks.local_justification: Verification step 2.1 explicitly identifies the two solutions for positive lambda and no real solutions for negative lambda.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Fold at (0,0), continuation arrows, filled point markers.
diagram_math_checks.check: The curve has vertical tangent in (lambda,x) coordinates at the origin, so its horizontal projection has zero derivative; both branch tips have arrows to indicate continuation rather than included/excluded endpoints. The fold and two marked preimages are included points, shown with filled cyan disks. This is an open curve segment depiction, with no graph-cycle or closure assertion.
diagram_math_checks.local_justification: Verification step 1.1 gives d(lambda)/dx=0 and d^2(lambda)/dx^2=2 at zero; step 3.1 checks the simple-fold conditions and the local supplier thm-simple-fold-lyapunov-schmidt-parameterization supplies the same curvature conclusion.
